security_audit.summary: Reviewed 29 static findings: most are false positives caused by markdown code fences, relative documentation links, and fixed memory paths. Confirmed the line 48 external command and network findings because the skill documents running a Firecrawl Python connector against user-supplied competitor targets. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Optional Firecrawl workflow launches an external Python connector and makes outbound network requests.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before network fetching, validate and quote competitor URLs, and offer an offline path using user-provided exports.

remediation.issue: Markdown prompt examples and inline paths trigger noisy command and filesystem scanner matches.
remediation.suggestion: Label prompt examples as non-shell text and keep write destinations constrained to the documented memory directory.

content.value_statement: Competitive SEO research often becomes scattered across keywords, links, content, and AI citations. This skill turns competitor evidence into a clear benchmark, gap list, and action plan.
actual_capabilities: Separates direct competitors, indirect alternatives, and content competitors for a market.
Benchmarks keyword rankings, top positions, intent mix, and keyword gaps.
Reviews content strategy, backlink profile, technical SEO, and traffic share.
Checks GEO and AI citation patterns for competitor visibility.
Labels metrics as measured, user-provided, estimated, or unavailable.
Produces a prioritized brief, comparison table, and immediate to long-term action plan.
limitations: It cannot measure private analytics without user exports or connected tools.
Estimated metrics depend on available public data and may need verification.
Detailed pairwise content gap mapping belongs in a separate content-gap workflow.
Live competitor fetching depends on connector availability and robots.txt permissions.

use_cases.title: Plan SEO Priorities
use_cases.description: Compare major competitors and choose keywords, pages, and link assets to prioritize next.

use_cases.title: Build Sales Battlecards
use_cases.description: Turn competitor positioning, strengths, weaknesses, and proof points into a clear battlecard.

use_cases.title: Benchmark AI Visibility
use_cases.description: Review where competitors appear in AI answers and identify citation-friendly content opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Competitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the SEO and GEO strategy for this competitor: [competitor URL]. Focus on visible strengths, weak spots, and three next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Several Competitors
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my site [your URL] against [competitor 1], [competitor 2], and [competitor 3]. Include keywords, content, backlinks, AI citations, and priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Find Exploitable Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [competitor list] for weaknesses we can exploit. Separate keyword gaps, content gaps, backlink gaps, and GEO citation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Evidence Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a competitor analysis brief for [market]. Label each metric as measured, user-provided, estimated, or unavailable, then create immediate, short-term, and long-term actions.

output_examples.input: Compare our B2B SaaS site with three search competitors.
output: A competitor set split into direct, indirect, and content competitors.
A benchmark covering authority, traffic, top keywords, backlinks, content cadence, and AI visibility.
A prioritized action plan with evidence labels for each recommendation.

output_examples.input: Why does one competitor rank for our most valuable topics?
output: A summary of their successful content patterns, linkable assets, and topic clusters.
A list of weaknesses to exploit, such as stale pages, generic advice, or missing niche depth.
Recommended pages, tools, or research assets to create next.

output_examples.input: Assess competitor visibility in AI answers for our category.
output: A query-by-query review of where competitors appear in AI responses.
The content formats and authority signals that appear to earn citations.
GEO content opportunities that your site can target.

best_practices: Provide competitor URLs, your own site URL, and the market segment before starting.
Treat estimated traffic, authority, and backlink numbers as directional until verified.
Use the final action plan to assign owners, deadlines, and evidence checks.
anti_patterns: Do not compare unrelated companies that serve different buyers or search intents.
Do not present model estimates as measured analytics or tool data.
Do not turn every competitor strength into a copycat recommendation.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes competitor keywords, content, backlinks, technical SEO, traffic share, positioning, and AI citation patterns.

faq.question: Does it need paid SEO tools?
faq.answer: No. It can work from user-provided data and public evidence, but paid tools improve metric confidence.

faq.question: Can it compare my site with competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide your site URL and competitor URLs for a benchmark table and prioritized action plan.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertain metrics?
faq.answer: It labels each metric as measured, user-provided, estimated, or unavailable, so assumptions stay visible.

faq.question: Is this the same as content gap analysis?
faq.answer: No. This skill gives a broad competitor benchmark. A dedicated content gap workflow is better for pairwise topic gaps.

faq.question: Can it support AI search optimization?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews AI citation patterns and suggests content formats that can improve GEO visibility.
